AMZN business-model profile (AI compute lens), 26 October 2026. Sources: 2025 10-K, 2Q26 release (30 July 2026), 2Q26 10-Q.

1. Engine: Amazon turns retail and ads cash flow plus investment-grade debt into data centers, chips and power, and rents that capacity through AWS on multi-year commitments. Its stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI double as anchor tenants.

2. Revenue map: AWS revenue = energized GW x utilization x price per unit of compute. Backlog (RPO): $244bn (4Q25), $364bn (1Q26), $496bn (2Q26), with a 6.4-year weighted life. AWS was $128.7bn in FY25 and $42.2bn in 2Q26 (+37%): 21% of revenue but 61% of segment operating income.

3. Costs: depreciation drives margins. AWS D&A was $21.5bn in FY25 and $8.1bn in 2Q26 (+67%). Servers last 5 to 6 years, with breakeven in under 3 per management. Other costs: power (270mn MWh of energy derivatives, about 15 years), leases and interest.

4. Funding: 2026 cash capex about $220bn (H1 net $96.3bn); AWS took 76% of H1 additions. Sources: OCF of $161.4bn TTM, about $92bn of notes March to July plus GBP 4.25bn in September (A1/AA/AA-), and an undrawn $17.5bn term loan, $20bn of revolvers and $30bn of CP. Long-term debt $133.0bn (year-end $68.8bn). Leases not yet commenced $137.2bn (year-end $96.4bn), with a parent rent guarantee at Cipher Stingray. TTM FCF -$7.6bn.

5. Sensitivities: power delivery timing, AI pricing, memory inflation, server lives, lab credit, bond spreads, and Anthropic marks ($190.4bn carrying value).

6. Position: largest cloud; Trainium and Graviton (chips run-rate above $25bn); multi-GW lab commitments. Power-short through 2027, so it is building on-site gas (GW Ranch) and signing nuclear deals. Rivals: Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle, neoclouds.

7. Breakers: the backlog stalls on power or chips; a lab cuts its commitments; AI prices fall faster than costs; capex outruns OCF and spreads widen; server lives shorten.
